# DraftLine

> DraftLine is free, open-source (MIT) screenwriting software for writing screenplays. It runs in a web browser on a computer or a phone, installs as a Progressive Web App, works offline and needs no account. Scripts stay on the writer's device. It is not a novel-writing app or a casting service.

- Website and app: https://draftlineapp.com/ (the address opens straight into the editor)
- Price: free; no subscription, no paid tier
- Licence: MIT; source at https://github.com/nanashi86/DraftLine
- Files: opens and saves Final Draft (.fdx) and Fountain (.fountain); exports PDF; imports PDF, Word and Google Docs
- Pagination: strict 54-line Hollywood pagination in 12-point Courier Prime, with (MORE) and (CONT'D)
- Phones: a 16px Courier Prime writing view, an element bar above the keyboard (Scene, Action, Character, Dialogue, Parenthetical, Transition), and page breaks identical to the desktop's, worked out at full page width
- Storage: in the browser on every device; linking a folder (including Google Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive folders) works in Chrome or Edge on a computer, not on phones
- Built for one writer: no real-time co-writing and no colored production revisions

## Pages

- [Features](https://draftlineapp.com/features/): every tool, including writing on a phone, the Scene Board, Format Doctor, Dialogue Tuner, Story Bible, snapshots, breakdowns, stripboard and reports
- [How DraftLine compares](https://draftlineapp.com/compare/): DraftLine beside Final Draft, Fade In, WriterDuet, Celtx and Beat, including where each of those is the better choice
- [README](https://github.com/nanashi86/DraftLine/blob/main/README.md): full documentation of every tool, keyboard shortcuts and file formats
